items.prompt_latex: If you invest \$100 at an interest rate of 5\% per year for 1 year, how much money will you have at the end of the year?
hint_ladder: Add the interest to the principal.
Use the formula: Final Amount = Principal + Interest.
items.targets_because: This item helps the student focus on simple interest calculation before introducing compound interest.

items.prompt_latex: If you invest \$100 at an interest rate of 5\% compounded annually for 2 years, how much money will you have at the end of the second year?
hint_ladder: Identify how many times the interest is applied.
Calculate the total amount using: Final Amount = Principal \times (1 + r)^n.
items.targets_because: This item introduces the context of compound interest over multiple periods, addressing the misconception directly.

items.prompt_latex: You deposit \$2000 in a bank account that offers 3\% interest compounded annually. How much will you have after 5 years?
hint_ladder: Calculate the growth factor for 5 years.
items.targets_because: This item reinforces the concept of compound interest over a longer time frame, solidifying understanding.

items.prompt_latex: If you invest \$1500 at an interest rate of 4\% compounded quarterly for 3 years, what will be the total amount at the end of the investment?
hint_ladder: Adjust the interest rate for quarterly compounding.
Use the formula: Final Amount = Principal \times (1 + \frac{r}{m})^{mt}.
items.targets_because: This item challenges the student to apply compound interest in a more complex scenario, enhancing their understanding.
